name: Granular Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Granular Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of discrete, sharply demarcated hyaline deposits in the corneal stroma visible on slit-lamp examination
Progressive decrease in visual acuity due to stromal opacities
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the TGFBI gene (commonly R555W mutation)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histopathological confirmation of hyaline deposits in corneal stroma if biopsy performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic corneal hyaline deposits on slit-lamp examination plus identification of pathogenic TGFBI mutation or compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from other corneal dystrophies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Discrete granular hyaline deposits in corneal stroma
pathognomonic.notes: Visible as white, breadcrumb-like opacities on slit-lamp exam

common.symptomName: Foreign body sensation in the eye

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying pathogenic TGFBI mutations (e.g., R555W)
Histopathology showing hyaline deposits in corneal stroma
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing granular stromal opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing hyperreflective stromal deposits
genetic: Autosomal dominant mutations in TGFBI gene
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Amyloid deposits forming lattice lines rather than granular hyaline deposits
More frequent recurrent erosions and corneal thinning
Diffuse stromal clouding with glycosaminoglycan deposits

redFlags: Rapid progression of corneal opacities leading to severe vision loss
Recurrent painful corneal erosions unresponsive to standard therapy
Secondary complications such as corneal ulceration or glaucoma
references: Klintworth GK. Corneal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:7.
Weiss JS, Møller HU, Aldave AJ, et al. IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies—edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
